drhp.business: Albert David Limited manufactures and trades pharmaceutical formulations, infusion solutions, herbal dosage forms and bulk drugs (APIs), and is the flagship company of the diversified Kothari Group, headquartered in Kolkata with operations across India and overseas. It has a longstanding presence in institutional and government supply segments and is positioned uniquely within the pharmaceutical landscape through its focus on infusion therapy.

risks.note: Supply chain challenges and elevated raw material or resource costs could adversely impact availability and overall product cost structure, resulting in diminished margins; company mitigates via alternative specifications/sourcing, inventory regulation for bulk discounts and price locking.
risks.risk: Material cost / raw material price volatility

risks.note: Geopolitical disruption could impact global supply chains and strain business-as-usual operations; the company is exposed to changes in input prices, international logistics, forex movements and availability of key starting materials, APIs, excipients and packaging materials.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption and global supply chain volatility

risks.note: By 2026 the pharmaceutical industry faces intense scrutiny over its carbon footprint; company categorises exposure into Physical Risks and Transition Risks and reviews its product portfolio for resilience against seasonal variability and climate change.

Intense pressure from both large-scale generic leaders (with large R&D budgets and economies of scale) and agile niche competitors; competitors are aggressively slashing prices in the Large Volume Parenterals (LVP) and IV fluid segments, risking irrational price behaviour industry-wide.

Unprecedented swings in foreign exchange rates driven by global geopolitical crisis may create short-term margin pressure from elevated material costs or depressed revenue realisations; the company is sensitive to the USD/INR exchange rate given its export operations.

Regulatory authorities are moving toward a risk-based approach across the pharma industry; drug establishment licenses, safety, health and environmental laws could change, negatively impacting operations, finances and business if compliance lags.

The Company operates in a single segment and therefore its performance could not be segregated in terms of business verticals or geographical presence, per Note No. 60 to the financial statements, indicating limited diversification.
